title: How Soon the Savior's Gracious Call
description: How Soon the Savior's Gracious Call in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 79, “Not in word, but in power”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How soon the Sa-vior's gra-cious call, Dis-armed the rage of bloo-dy Saul! Je-sus, the knowl-edge of thy name, Chan-ges the li-on to a lamb!

lines: How soon the Savior's gracious call,
Disarmed the rage of bloody Saul!
Jesus, the knowledge of thy name,
Changes the lion to a lamb!
Zaccheus, when he knew the Lord,
What he had gained by wrong, restored;
And of the wealth he prized before,
He gave the half to feed the poor.
The woman who so vile had been,
When brought to weep o'er pardoned sin,
Was from her evil ways estranged,
And showed that grace her heart had changed.
And can we think the pow'r of grace
Is lost, by change of time and place?
Then it was mighty, all allow,
And is it but a notion now?
Can they whom pride and passion sway,
Who Mammon and the world obey,
In envy or contention live,
Presume that they indeed believe?
True faith unites to Christ the root,
By him producing holy fruit;
And they who no such fruit can show,
Still on the stock of nature grow.
Lord, let thy word effectual prove,
To work in us obedient love!
And may each one who hears it dread
A name to live; and yet be dead.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
